ownership_rule: Temporary field formations own no people. They reference exact existing deployed faction members and cannot duplicate them.
headcount_rule: Every commander and deputy is one of the deployed people and is included in deployed headcount.
scale_rule: Use the smallest lawful top-level formation for the actual deployment. Do not wrap a Team, Section or Wing in a redundant Field Force headquarters.
standing_office_rule: A faction's standing field_commander and deputy_field_commander are preferred top-command candidates for Wing/Field Force deployments only when those exact office-holders are actually deployed. Temporary field command and standing institutional office remain separate facts.
deputy_rule: Top-level Sections, Wings and Field Forces use a deputy when headcount permits. Nested child formations normally use one commander because the parent headquarters already provides command redundancy. A child detached to operate independently is rebuilt as its own top-level formation and then gains the lawful deputy slot.

party.command: one lead person for coordination when needed; no deputy

section.command: section leader; top-level section also uses a deputy

wing.command: wing commander plus deputy at top level

examples.5_people: one Team led by one of the five; no higher headquarters
examples.24_people: one Section with Section Leader and Deputy; no Field Force wrapper
examples.80_people: one Wing with Wing Commander and Deputy plus subordinate Sections led by Section Leaders
examples.180_people: one Field Force with Field Commander and Deputy plus multiple subordinate Wings; no separate Sword-style Unit Commander layer

command_rule: Command changes coordination, order latency, synchronization, reserve employment, pursuit, protection, extraction and withdrawal. It never directly increases physical attributes, martial skills, Qi or damage.
team_tactics_rule: Formal field command sets objective, priorities and coordination. The exact-combat team tactical planner may create temporary exchange roles such as screen, intercept, pressure, protect and exploit without creating a second permanent command hierarchy.
